clue.text: Benefits from book by novelist, Doris's last

indicators.note: the last of a name means only its closing letter is kept

blocks.note: B is the standard abbreviation for book
Doris Lessing, the Nobel-winning British novelist
the final letter of the name Doris

explanation.surface: Someone reaps rewards from a book by Doris Lessing, her last one.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Doris's last' as her final novel, but the novelist is Doris Lessing and 'Doris's last' is just the closing letter of her first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Blessings are good things received, so they are benefits or advantages in the plural noun sense.

clue.text: Reverse taxi over, parking at centre

indicators.note: turned over means the vehicle's letters are read backwards
the centre of a word is its middle letter, the only one kept

blocks.note: a cab is a taxi
the middle letter of this seven-letter word

explanation.surface: An instruction to back a taxi up and park it in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverse taxi' reads as driving instructions, but Reverse is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To back is to move in reverse, as a driver backs a car out of a space.

clue.text: Moved abroad - good being in Dubai, for example, with daughter

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one letter goes within a word

blocks.note: Dubai is one of the United Arab Emirates
G is the abbreviation for good
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Someone relocated overseas: it is fine living in Dubai with a daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: To emigrate is to leave one's country to live elsewhere, so emigrated means moved overseas.

clue.text: Groucho's Bar playing show song

indicators.note: playing suggests something in motion and rearranged, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: the letters of these words, apostrophe ignored
a fair is a show or exhibition, as in a trade fair

explanation.surface: A bar named after Groucho Marx is staging a musical number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show song' looks like one phrase, a showtune; it splits into wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarborough Fair is a traditional English ballad made famous by Simon and Garfunkel.

clue.text: Turning brown - Russian river, as is to be expected

indicators.note: turning round means the colour word is read backwards

blocks.note: tan is a shade of brown
the Ural river flows from Russia to the Caspian

explanation.surface: Turning brown in the Russian river is only to be expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning brown' reads as a colour change, but Turning works on the colour word.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural means normal or unsurprising, in the sense of what one would expect to happen.

clue.text: Star member up in tanning area?

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: the sun is a star
a member is a part of a whole

explanation.surface: A star's limb is raised while sunbathing.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is playful: a suntrap is a sheltered sunny spot, here viewed as where people tan.
explanation.definitionFit: A suntrap is a sunny, sheltered place, ideal for sunbathing and getting a tan.

clue.text: Shoot bishop after all others

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
coming after everyone else is being last

explanation.surface: A gunman fires at the bishop once everyone else has been dealt with.
explanation.walkthrough: The bishop comes first in the answer even though 'after' seems to place it later; 'after all others' is a single phrase meaning last.
explanation.definitionFit: To blast is to fire a gun or shoot at something, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Gunner grabbed unexpectedly, crossing at a landmark near to Checkpoint Charlie

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests things turning out in a surprising order, so letters are reworked
crossing means spanning over, so the shuffled letters take in the little word

blocks.note: the letters of these two words
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier is unexpectedly seized while crossing near the famous Berlin border post.
explanation.walkthrough: Gunner looks like a soldier subject, but it and grabbed supply letters; Checkpoint Charlie was the Cold War crossing point in Berlin.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brandenburg Gate is the neoclassical monument in central Berlin, close to the old Checkpoint Charlie.

clue.text: I travel, giving support to a male friend

blocks.note: A plus M, the abbreviation for male
I plus go, which means travel

explanation.surface: A traveller helps out a male companion.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, a piece giving support sits underneath, so the travel piece goes below the male piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend and is used informally in English for a pal.

clue.text: Fail to make any progress, as war treated suspiciously

indicators.note: something handled suspiciously is treated as dodgy or not straight, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A conflict handled with distrust ends in deadlock.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread water is an idiom for staying in the same place without advancing, like a swimmer keeping afloat.

clue.text: Punch a mate

blocks.note: to chin someone is to punch them on the jaw
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to hit a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: China means friend via Cockney rhyming slang: 'china plate' rhymes with mate.
explanation.definitionFit: In British rhyming slang 'china plate' stands for mate, so china is an informal word for a pal.

clue.text: Big top musical? Backing provisional

indicators.note: going backwards means the show title is read from end to start

blocks.note: the big top is the circus tent
Evita, the Lloyd Webber musical

explanation.surface: A circus show set to music gets only tentative financial backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like money or musical accompaniment, but it turns the musical round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tentative is not yet final or certain, just as a provisional arrangement is.

clue.text: Actor, in the guise of Scottish king, about to wade across behind duke

indicators.note: behind means coming after, so the wading piece is placed second, after the duke's letter

blocks.note: Robert the Bruce and other Scottish kings named Robert
re means about or concerning
D is the abbreviation for duke
to ford a river is to wade across it

explanation.surface: An actor plays a Scottish king who wades a river behind a duke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind duke' puts the wading word after the duke's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Redford is the American film star of Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid, so an example of an actor.

clue.text: Chief city in Middle East - large container port set up

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means raised so the words read from bottom to top

blocks.note: ME is the abbreviation for Middle East
a silo is a large storage tower for grain
taken as written

explanation.surface: A major Middle Eastern city has a big container port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'large container port' reads as a shipping terminal, but it splits into a storage tower and the word port.
explanation.definitionFit: A metropolis is the main or capital city of a country or region.

clue.text: Drunk loiters in a Portuguese resort

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so the following word's letters reel into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunk hangs about in a holiday town in Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: Estoril is a seaside resort on the coast west of Lisbon in Portugal.

clue.text: An expert in Pennsylvania helps to produce a universal remedy

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside the state's letters

blocks.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania
taken as written
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A specialist in Pennsylvania helps develop a cure-all.
explanation.definitionFit: A panacea is a supposed cure for all ills, the very meaning of a universal remedy.

clue.text: Humiliated Conservative hurried

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
hastened means hurried

explanation.surface: A Tory politician rushed off in disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: Chastened means subdued or humbled after a rebuke, close in sense to humiliated.

clue.text: Ruby? Girl in former tin mining town

blocks.note: ruby is a shade of red
a girl's name

explanation.surface: Is a girl called Ruby living in an old Cornish mining town?
explanation.walkthrough: Ruby looks like a girl's name but is the colour; the girl comes next. Redruth is a town in Cornwall, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Redruth in Cornwall was once a centre of the tin mining industry, now closed.

clue.text: Hornblower's short speech after end of skirmish

definitions.note: possessive: the answer is the first name belonging to Hornblower

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept
cut short means the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: the final letter of this word
an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A naval hero makes a brief address after a minor battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Horatio Hornblower is C. S. Forester's fictional Napoleonic-era naval officer; 'Hornblower's' stands for his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio is the given name of Forester's hero, so it is the name that is Hornblower's own.

clue.text: Vulgar about Salvation Army campaign

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: crude means vulgar or coarse
SA is the abbreviation for the Salvation Army

explanation.surface: A coarse remark is made about the Salvation Army's fundraising drive.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusade is a vigorous campaign for a cause, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Group from lake bed shown first

blocks.note: a cot is a small bed
Lake Erie, one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A party gathered from a lake bed shown on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown first' tells you the bed word goes before the lake, reversing the clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small exclusive circle of people with shared interests.

clue.text: Baffling drama? Pretend not to be interested

blocks.note: a play is a drama
something baffling is hard to get, that is, hard to understand

explanation.surface: A confusing stage piece prompts an audience to feign indifference.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are read in reverse of their clue order: the drama comes first, then the word for baffling.
explanation.definitionFit: To play hard to get is an idiom for feigning a lack of romantic or other interest to seem more desirable.

clue.text: Girl, one interrupting queen

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: Queen Anne of Great Britain
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A girl cuts in on the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Annie is a female first name, so an example of a girl.

clue.text: Exploited group in House, Democrats

indicators.note: a group of letters in a word means a run of them is lifted from inside it

blocks.note: the last three letters of this word
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: A faction in the House of Representatives, the Democrats, was taken advantage of.
explanation.walkthrough: House looks like the US chamber, but it just supplies its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit someone is to use them for one's own ends, so exploited and used are verb synonyms.

clue.text: House in historic city

blocks.note: first meaning: the royal dynasty of England that fought York in the Wars of the Roses
second meaning: the county town of Lancashire in north-west England

explanation.surface: A dwelling sits inside an old city.
explanation.walkthrough: House here means a royal dynasty, not a building.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a medieval English royal dynasty and to an old city in north-west England.

clue.text: Miss Grey, a long time entertaining knight

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: ages means a long time
N is the chess abbreviation for knight

explanation.surface: A Miss Grey has been hosting a knight for a long while.
explanation.walkthrough: Agnes Grey is the title heroine of Anne Brontë's first novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnes is the first name of the governess heroine of Anne Brontë's novel Agnes Grey.

clue.text: Box containing English throwing weapon

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: to spar is to box in practice
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A crate holds an English missile.
explanation.walkthrough: Box looks like a container noun but is the verb for sparring.
explanation.definitionFit: A spear is a long pointed weapon that can be thrown, like a javelin.

clue.text: Began to check boundary not rigorously fixed

indicators.note: to check something is to hold it in, so one word is held inside another

blocks.note: opened means began
an end is a limit or boundary

explanation.surface: Someone started to inspect a perimeter that was never properly set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to check' looks like the purpose of beginning, but it tells you the first word restrains the second inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open-ended has no set limits or conclusion, so it is flexible rather than firmly determined.
